hook: A U.S. Air Force ISR aircraft from the 124th Attack Squadron, operating under USCENTCOM in the Gulf of Aden, observed a single UAP on July 14, 2024 at 0517Z while conducting target development for NAVCENT. The object outpaced the observing aircraft on a straight northwest flight path before the crew lost tracking range.
why_it_matters: This MISREP is notable because it was formally routed through USCENTCOM's mandatory declassification review and approved for release directly to AARO, illustrating the post-2022 institutional pipeline for military UAP reporting. The document captures a live ISR crew encounter during an active intelligence-collection mission, lending it operational context uncommon in historical UAP files. The observer's own assessment — 'benign' — and the structured AARO reporting fields (propulsion, intelligent control, advanced capabilities all marked 'UNKNOWN') reflect the standardized post-NDAA UAP data-collection framework in practice.
key_findings: UAP was observed at 140517ZJUL24 with a straight flight path at the same altitude and a speed exceeding the observing aircraft; the crew followed it until it flew beyond tracking range.
The observer, a TSGT/E-5 from 124 ATKS (132 Wing, Air Force), assessed the UAP as 'benign'; no effects on persons or equipment were recorded, and no material was recovered.
UAP trajectory was northwest at low kinetic altitude; first and last coordinates are partially redacted but span grid squares 38P MT 53 and 38P MT 22, indicating measurable lateral displacement.
Full Motion Video (FMV) was the primary sensor and was exploited post-mission, but all descriptive fields for the UAP's physical appearance are redacted under exemption 1.4a/1.4g.

UAP propulsion means, intelligent control status, and advanced capabilities are all formally recorded as 'UNKNOWN,' consistent with AARO's standardized MISREP fields, and no RF signatures or interrogation returns were captured.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: The document is explicitly stamped 'Approved for Release to AARO' and uses AARO's standardized UAP reporting fields throughout the UAP section, making AARO the direct institutional recipient of this report.
The document carries a SECRET//REL TO USA, FVEY classification caveat throughout all pages, meaning it was authorized for sharing across all Five Eyes partner nations.
